headline: The material system was already there, the characters already declared their material variants, and nothing was reading them. All seventeen CHARACTER_SPECS carry `material: { skin, cloth, palette, wear }` with wear from 0.15 to 0.95 and a region palette on every one; `ensureBuilt` consumed two of the four and `palette` and `wear` reached no frame. On top of that the body's UVs were parametric — `u = i/radial`, `v = t*2`, no metres in them — so the authored linen and hide were pasted 5.52x too fine and the mip chain resolved them to their own mean colour. That is the whole of 'one flat colour of cloth over one flat colour of skin'.

the_diagnosis_and_how_it_was_derived.the_reading_i_started_with_was_wrong: The obvious reading of the round-2 finding is 'the characters have no textures'. They always had them. `game/src/render/scene.js:98` builds `mats.skin` and `mats.cloth` through `worldMaterial()`; `ls game/assets/w1-30/materials/rough_linen/` returns three files and `brown_leather/` three more. The maps were bound the whole time.
the_diagnosis_and_how_it_was_derived.instrument: `tools/visual/character-texel-density.mjs` (new). Per body mesh, per triangle: world area in m^2 against UV area in uv^2, area-weighted, giving metres per UV unit and hence metres per texture tile against `TEXEL_METRES[family] / repeat`. `--self-test` builds a quad whose UVs are correct by construction, asserts ratio 1.00, then multiplies its UVs by 8 and asserts the tool reports 8.00 — it GOES RED. `repeat` is 2 because `authoredMaps()`'s `setup()` sets `t.repeat.set(2,2)`; node has no `document` so the browser path cannot be read off a material built here, and the tool takes it as an argument rather than guessing.
the_diagnosis_and_how_it_was_derived.before: 13 subjects, 26 body meshes. saxhleel:skin 0.127 m/tile against a 0.700 target = 5.52x TOO DENSE. humanoid:skin 5.06x. saxhleel:cloth 2.53x. humanoid:cloth 2.35x. 4 of 4 surfaces outside a 2x band; exit 1.
the_diagnosis_and_how_it_was_derived.after: 13 subjects, 39 body meshes. Worst deviation 1.15x. 0 of 6 outside the band; exit 0.
the_diagnosis_and_how_it_was_derived.why_that_produces_flatness_specifically: A 1 k texture at 0.127 m per tile is eight texels to the millimetre. At every framing a player meets — 2 m conversation, 8-10 m gameplay — the selected mip is far up the chain and what reaches the screen is the texture's own mean colour. The map is bound, sampled, and invisible.
the_diagnosis_and_how_it_was_derived.the_declaration_that_was_never_wired: `lib/rigs.js` declares `material` as a variant axis and `variantKey()` hashes `palette`, `skin`, `cloth` and `wear` into the census identity that counts our seventeen characters as distinct. `ensureBuilt` read `mat.skin` and `mat.cloth` as tint hexes and dropped the other two on the floor. Verified by reading the call: `buildSkeleton(rigSource, A.mats, tintHex, skinHex, A.artFamily, spec && spec.morph)` — six arguments, no material.

what_changed.what: `MeshBuilder` takes `mpt` (its family's `TEXEL_METRES`) and every primitive unwraps against it — tube `u` is arc length at mean radius and `v` is distance along, ball and ellipsoid are equirectangular in metres. This is `MATERIAL_API.md` §5's stated seam and exactly what `lib/kits.js` has always done (`p[axis] / mpt`); the character was the one surface in the game that ignored it.
what_changed.the_detail_that_is_easy_to_get_wrong: Tube cap centres are placed a TRUE RADIUS away in UV on the `v` axis, so a cap triangle has UV area pi*r^2/mpt^2 against a world area of pi*r^2 — the same density as the wall it closes. The old `[.5,.5]` collapsed every cap to a UV sliver, which reads to a density instrument, and to the mip selector, as infinitely coarse.
what_changed.measured: 5.52x -> 1.12x on skin, 2.53x -> 1.09x on cloth. See above.

what_changed.id: 2. the variant's own palette and wear, at last consumed
what_changed.what: `buildSkeleton` takes the material spec and builds the body surfaces through `worldMaterial(family, { palette, wear, wearFrom: 'geometry', vertexColors: true })`, banked by (family, palette, wear) so 408 NPCs cost at most seventeen materials plus a clone each for tint and waterline uniforms.
what_changed.wearFrom_geometry_is_an_answer_to_a_writ: `MATERIAL_API.md` §6a is addressed to this file by name: 'Bake `esCurvature` onto your kit parts and your rigs ... and pass `wearFrom: geometry`. The option is frozen and live now ... this is the only route to the plan's `wear reads` gate.' `bakeCurvature()` has been running at the bottom of `MeshBuilder.build()` the whole time, writing that attribute with nothing reading it. Now it is read.
what_changed.why_the_bank_is_in_actor_js_and_not_scen: `mats.cloth` and `mats.skin` are SHARED — `places.js` hangs market awnings off `mats.cloth` and `scene.js`'s showcase builds a static villager from `mats.skin`. Turning `vertexColors` on there would multiply an awning by a vertex colour it does not have, and three.js reads a missing `color` attribute as undefined rather than as white. So the body surfaces get their own bank and the world materials are untouched.

what_changed.id: 3. the garment, painted per vertex — zero triangles, zero draw calls
what_changed.what: `paintBody()` writes a per-vertex colour over the finished surface in rest space, against landmarks read off the rig rather than retyped (pelvis 0.980, spine_00 1.100, spine_02 1.340, knee 0.510, ankle 0.090). Cloth: a shoulder yoke, a two-wrap sash, a tunic hem, a legging cuff, four vertical seams measured in ARC length so a seam is 12 mm wide on a narrow arm and 12 mm wide on a broad chest, a leggings panel tone, and a damp/dirt gradient rising from the hem. Skin: pale-ventral / dark-dorsal countershading off the normal's z, scale rows at 34 mm pitch on the reptilian family only, and a paler throat.
what_changed.why_vertex_colour_and_not_a_second_textu: A second texture set for a family we already have is a `visual-foundation` census `duplicate` by construction (MATERIAL_API §4). More geometry costs triangles on a body already at 28,136 against a 12,000 bar. A vertex colour costs three floats, multiplies the authored albedo rather than replacing it — so the linen weave still reads underneath the panel it belongs to — and lives on the SHARED BODY PLAN, so it improves all seventeen characters in one edit.

what_changed.id: 4. a third body surface, and it is Argonia's vocabulary rather than Skyrim's
what_changed.what: Cord lashing (cloth family, three rings per forearm and two per shin) and bone fittings (a new `bone` skinned surface: a sash toggle and two shoulder clasps).
what_changed.the_design_call_and_why_the_obvious_one_: The Skyrim full-body plates I opened (`REF-CF-SK__skyrim-leather-armor-male-fullbody.png`) are all buckles, straps, rivets and a metal belt disc, and copying that read is EXACTLY what `RI-VIS10` §D2 forbids: 'buckled leather jerkin with bracers' is on the generic-fantasy list that must occur ZERO times, and three occurrences cap the item at 3. The modern plates are routed FIDELITY-ONLY (refs/characters/INDEX.md §4) — they govern how WELL a thing is made, not what it is. So the fittings are §D3's Black Marsh vocabulary — lashed cord and bone — and the ESO Argonian plate, which shows corded wraps running wrist to elbow on both arms, is cited for construction and not as a target.
what_changed.and_it_is_what_makes_B3_answerable_at_al: RI-VIS08 B3 asks for '>= 3 materially distinct regions' whose specular delta differs by >= 2x between highest and lowest. A body with exactly two surfaces cannot answer that question however well those two are made. Now there are three, with genuinely different roughness and response: cloth (rough_linen), skin (brown_leather), bone (marble_01).

the_capture_defect_the_orchestrator_flag.the_cause_read_out_of_the_engine_not_inf: `game/src/engine.js:11517` — `listEntities() { ... for (const n of this.sim.npcs) out.push({ ..., pos: [...] }) }`. IT IS NOT RANGE-FILTERED. It returns every NPC in the simulation wherever it is. Both existing capture tools log `stand X: N npc(s) in range` and then take the first N in LIST ORDER. There is no 'in range' — the phrase is the whole bug.
the_capture_defect_the_orchestrator_flag.the_base_rate_and_it_is_far_worse_than_a: Measured this run, three stands: char-player 60 enumerated / 27 within 80 m, street-lilmoth 60 / 27, street-gideon 109 / 27. **148 of 229 enumerated NPCs — 64.6% — are not where the stand is.** Round 2's 'two of seven' and the sweep's '17 of 93' were not a rare bug; they were the tail of a majority.
the_capture_defect_the_orchestrator_flag.the_fix_is_selection_not_detection: A liveness gate that rejects the frame afterwards has already paid for it. `selectByProximity()` measures every enumerated NPC's distance from its stand, SORTS BY IT AND TAKES THE NEAREST — which is what 'in range' was supposed to mean — rejects anything beyond `--max-offset`, and publishes the whole distribution. Both arms independently selected the same five subjects at offsets 0, 11.1, 12.8, 14.5 and 14.8 m, and both wrote 148 rejections.
the_capture_defect_the_orchestrator_flag.the_threshold_is_now_calibrated_against_: I could NOT calibrate it offline — `game/data/npcs/*.json` carries a position on 0 of 408 records, because placement is a run-time property of the sim — so I shipped it DECLARED at 80 m with its provenance stated, and made every run publish the population. The run then calibrated it: the largest gap in the sorted distances is 58.1 -> 5717.8 m at char-player, 60.4 -> 5750.7 m at lilmoth, 63.2 -> 2963.7 m at gideon. The nearest 27 subjects at every stand sit between 11 m and 63 m; the next one is between 2.9 km and 5.7 km away. **80 m sits in a measured gap roughly three orders of magnitude wider than the band it separates.** It is no longer a guess.
the_capture_defect_the_orchestrator_flag.self_test: `node tools/visual/f10-r3-materials.mjs --self-test` keeps a subject 3.6 m from the stand, rejects one at 2233.7 m, and then — the arm that must disagree — lifts the threshold and keeps BOTH, proving the rejection is the threshold doing work rather than a coincidence. Exit 0.
the_capture_defect_the_orchestrator_flag.what_i_did_NOT_do: I did not fix `f10-character-sweep.mjs` or `f10-r2-appearance.mjs`. Both are CLAIMED by live piece W1-30V (ownership run, not assumed). `selectByProximity` is exported from my file for exactly that adoption.
